current_difficulty_reason: The assumed Penrose lower bound alone does not provide density decay or a scattering profile uniform as hbar tends to zero. The author supplies the full quantum Lindhard derivative and Green-function inversion estimates, then uses the source-specific free-density convolution to control the interacting density. The complete finite-difference, weighted Fourier-variable and tail-integral argument closes the moving quantum Sobolev scattering estimate with uniform constants, rather than treating that new semiclassical estimate as a standard prerequisite.
closure: Selected original Proposition2.11 linear density phase mixing and scattering under assumed uniform Penrose condition. Retain d>=3, exact M=ceil((d+1)/2), short-range real w, weighted g/Qin hypotheses and exact quantum Sobolev/Fourier-Wigner normalization. Selected N0,N1 are nonnegative integers satisfying N1<N0-d/2-1; this is an explicit restriction of the carrier constants1363 to match the printed integer inverse-Laplace derivative count1339. No nonlinear bootstrap, Coulomb, independently established quantum-to-classical scattering limit or Penrose-sufficiency criterion is selected. Complete source-written Lindhard/Green/resolvent, density convolution, finite-difference and scattering-profile integral core retained.
